name: LMH6642 / LMH6643 / LMH6644
tagline: Low-power 130 MHz, ±75 mA rail-to-rail-output buffer in FiiO and iBasso gear; Head-Fi rollers call it warm and relaxed.

lineage.note: LMH high-speed line. Original date May 2001 (rev O prints May 2004). Early title began '3V, Low Power'.
Acquired National in 2011. Datasheet reissued as SNOS966 (revs O, P, Q), now titled 'LMH664x'.

part_numbers.note: Single, SOT-23-5 (MF) and SOIC-8 (MA). Leaded LMH6642MF (no /NOPB) is NRND.
Dual, SOIC-8 (MA) and VSSOP-8 (MM). The FiiO / iBasso part.
Quad, SOIC-14 (MA) and TSSOP-14 (MT). Leaded non-NOPB variants probably NRND (unconfirmed).

key_specs.value: Bipolar; CM range V− −0.5 V to V+ −1 V; RRO 40 mV
key_specs.condition: typ; output swing at light load

reputation.summary: Known from portable OEM gear and Head-Fi rolling, not classic hi-fi. FiiO used it as the E10K headphone buffer (replacing the AD8397); iBasso used it stock. Users call it warm and relaxed, 'hard to beat for buffers' into low impedances; others say it lacks some impact. All subjective forum impressions.
typical_uses: Headphone buffer in FiiO E10K, X3-II, X5, E18; iBasso D-series
Buffer after DAC I/V or gain stage at low supplies
caveats: 12.8 V maximum supply (about ±6.4 V): never roll into ±15 V sockets.
17 nV/√Hz is noisy versus NE5532 or LME49720; suits buffers, not low-level gain stages.
130 MHz part: layout and decoupling matter; capacitive loads may need an isolation resistor.
Some iBasso units reportedly shipped with THS4032 instead; FiiO X3-II/X5/E18 use is forum-reported.
Users preferring LME49721 or OPA2727 report less 'impact and boldness' as a buffer.

counterfeit_notes: No LMH664x-specific counterfeit or remarking reports. Parts are cheap and widely stocked. Leaded non-NOPB codes (e.g. LMH6642MF) are older NRND production with a different lead finish, not fakes. Treat marketplace SOIC/VSSOP parts with usual caution.

open_questions: Is SNOS966Q (Sep 2014) still the latest, or has TI issued R or later?
What do the change logs of revisions O, P and Q say? What National DS number and revisions preceded O?
Why does rev O print an original date of May 2004 while P and Q print May 2001?
Do generic TI PCNs (e.g. PCN20220127001, FFAB fab qualification) cover the LMH664x? No die change identified so far.
Which FiiO models (X3-II, X5, E18) actually used the LMH6643? Currently forum-reported only.

claims_confirmed: SNOS966Q, revised September 2014, is hosted by TI (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/snos966q/snos966q.pdf).
Current TI title is 'LMH664x Low Power, 130 MHz, 75 mA Rail-to-Rail Output Amplifiers' (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/lmh6643.pdf).
National-era title was 'LMH6642/6643/6644 3V, Low Power, 130MHz, 75mA Rail-to-Rail Output Amplifiers' (https://www.farnell.com/datasheets/4902.pdf).
LMH6642, LMH6643, LMH6644 are single, dual, quad (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/snos966q/snos966q.pdf).
corrections: Statuses changed from unknown to active; leaded LMH6642MF is NRND.
Added SNOS966 revisions O (Jan 2012), P (Mar 2013), Q (Sep 2014) and mirrors preserving older revisions.
Output current is ±75 mA linear per datasheet, not 'about 75 mA'.
Added supply caveat: 12.8 V maximum rules out ±15 V sockets.
No LMH664x-specific PCN or die change found.
